
### consistency  {.smaller}

![](/routing-ls/texfig/sp-consistency.figure.svg){fig-alt="network where A has two paths to C. One via B and one other node, and one via two other nodes."}
 

* if A sends packet for C to B, how does A know B won't send it back? 
<hr class="vspace" />
* hope: if A thought shortest path to C was through B, then B should agree
* problem: not always true


### inconsistency 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}
![](/routing-ls/texfig/sp-inconsistency.figure-1.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="Same network, but the link from C toward B has just gone down,"}

![](/routing-ls/texfig/sp-inconsistency.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="The information about the down link propogates to B and from C to the next node on the other path, but has not reached A yet."}

:::


::: {.myoverbox .fragment .fade-in fragment-index=2}

*  B thinks best route to C: through A 
*  A thinks best route to C: through B

:::


### temporary bad routes  {.smaller}


* while waiting for link state updates to propogate
* can have too-slow routes
* can have routing loops 
<hr class="vspace" />
* hope: this is only a few seconds at most 

   * and routing loop doesn't cause huge explosion of traffic
